Team — quick summary of what I'm seeing from infra metrics:

- Around 07:48 PDT we observed a sudden increase in queued inference requests tied to Finex's route.
- GPU utilization on the hosted pool ramped to 98–100% for several pods. Autoscaler added nodes, but node total lagged request surge by ~2–3 minutes due to slow instance initialization and model load time for the quantized variant.
- Result: transient KV cache thrash and OOM/5xx from the runtime as eviction + load churn hit at the same time.

Immediate mitigations I recommend and will enact now:
1) Scale the overflow dedicated pool for Finex (if available) and hot-swap routing for 10% traffic.
2) Force-deploy warmed model instance (preloaded checkpoint) to reduce cold-starts for that model family.
3) Apply a short-term rate-limit/fail-fast for heavy batched requests (we'll hit 429s intentionally for a controlled period rather than letting backend hit OOM).

I'm pushing the warmed instance and requesting capacity swap. I'll update with timing.

- Dev
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Executive summary for records and for Legal/Finance review:

- Incident window: 07:48–09:05 PDT (spike start to error-rate normalization).
- Impact: Finex experienced sustained elevated 5xx/429s and latency spikes; customer reduced retries per request which prevented larger outage.
- Root cause: Rapid traffic ramp + hosted GPU pool saturation + autoscaler lead time + model cold-starts for that model variant. No code bug — capacity/operational gap.
- Actions taken: overflow routing (10% traffic), warmed-instance deploys, temporary controlled throttles, customer retry guidance.
